Summary Collaboration Themes: This collaboration bridges the gap between peripheral physiological drivers (exercise, nutrition, muscle-brain axis) and central molecular mechanisms of neural plasticity and disease (ubiquitination, ER stress, mGluR signaling). By combining Rhodes' expertise in behavioral genetics, nutritional genomics, and in vivo exercise models with Tsai's specialization in molecular neuroscience, ubiquitin-proteasome systems, and electrophysiology, the partnership aims to uncover how lifestyle factors modulate synaptic protein turnover and network excitability. This synergy offers novel insights into the molecular basis of neurodevelopmental disorders, addiction, and the therapeutic potential of non-pharmacological interventions like exercise and diet.
